question: Which problems in large language models remain unresolved, and in which application areas are LLMs already used, with how do the challenges constrain them?
contributions: A systematic set of 16 open challenges grouped into Design, Behavior and Science (Fig 1).

An overview of applications in chatbots, computational biology, programming, creative work, knowledge work, law, medicine, reasoning, robotics, social sciences and synthetic data, with the constraint each faces.

limits: Self-described as an 'opinionated review' that assumes familiarity with LLMs (Sec 1).
Covers models trained on text data only and omits political, philosophical and moral perspectives (Sec 1).
Table 2 is non-exhaustive and reports only the largest size per paper; tokenizer entries marked SP could not be resolved to BPE or Unigram.
Literature cutoff July 2023 (arXiv v1, 19 Jul 2023): LLaMA 2 is the latest model in Table 2; scaling, long-context, alignment and evaluation statements have dated.
Every number is quoted from other work; the survey runs no experiments of its own.
practices: Run controlled ablations varying one factor at a time (e.g. model size or context length) when training new LLMs (Sec 2.15).
Use zero-shot hyperparameter transfer (muP) from small to large models as a cheaper ablation route; verified only up to 6.7B (Sec 2.15).
Report full performance distributions across runs rather than aggregate point estimates (Sec 2.15).
Prefer open-source LLMs for repeatable inference, since API models change and are stochastic even at temperature zero (Sec 2.16).
Consider inference cost, not only training cost, when choosing model size; train smaller models on more tokens (Sec 2.3).
Evaluate multiple-choice benchmarks with a fixed protocol, since results change with evaluation method and prompt (Sec 2.11).
Use an API definition in the prompt, or modular prompting, to fit long code or story tasks into a context window (Sec 3.3, Fig 13, Fig 14).

terms.definition: discrepancies between the data that a tokenizer and a model have been trained on can lead to glitch tokens [465], which can subsequently cause unexpected model behavior as their corresponding embeddings are essentially untrained
Tokenizers introduce several challenges, e.g., computational overhead, language dependence, handling of novel words, fixed vocabulary size, information loss, and low human interpretability.
The size of modern pre-training datasets renders it impractical for any individual to read or conduct quality assessments on the encompassed documents thoroughly.
occurs when the training dataset contains data from or similar to the evaluation test set
Generated text that is fluent and natural but unfaithful to the source content (intrinsic) and/or under-determined (extrinsic).
the phenomenon of task performance worsening as model scale and training loss performance increases
the ability to repeat experimental outcomes exactly
how often a model can correctly answer all sub-problems but not generate the overall solution
